purpose: Forest furniture preview at AMOLED native display dimensions

prompts.name: bowl-forest-empty-v1
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: independent transparent furniture sprite for StickMon, a cozy small-screen creature-care game. Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and defines the exact object category, camera, orientation and approximate silhouette. Input image 2 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: the user's approved forest leaf bed. Create a matching forest-themed replacement of image 1. Match image 2's hand-painted pixel-art-inspired game rendering, crisp warm dark stepped outlines, restrained detailed wicker/wood craft, broad sage and moss green leaves, honey-brown wood and soft cream highlights. This is the detailed original forest style, not a coarse pixel prototype and not photorealistic. Design must read at tiny in-game size. Composition: one complete isolated object, centered with transparent padding, no clipping. Preserve target camera and projected orientation. Real transparent alpha outside the object; no white backdrop, checkerboard, room, wall, floor, platform, labels, text, UI, watermark, characters or extra furniture. No cast shadow outside the object; self shading allowed. 
Specific design: Replace the mint paw-print bowl with an EMPTY low round ceramic pet food bowl in sage green, broad elliptical open mouth, warm cream inner basin and rim. One broad raised leaf motif centered on the front, restrained honey wood accent foot. IMPORTANT remove all berries, all food and any garnish; the bowl must be completely empty so the game can draw food separately. Keep proportions about 1.45 wide to 1 high, elevated front view, no stem, no tall decoration. Readable when only 20 logical pixels wide.

prompts.name: window-forest-day-v1
prompts.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: single transparent forest-themed WINDOW DAY sprite for a tiny handheld game. Input image 1 is the exact geometry/camera reference and EDIT TARGET; input image 2 is approved forest bed material/color STYLE REFERENCE. Redesign the circular wood window in image 1 to belong with the forest bed, preserving the target's right-wall perspective and silhouette: a near-oval honey-brown round wooden frame, vertical wooden mullion, crossbar slants DOWN to image right. A few LARGE SIMPLE sage leaves hug the frame (not a wreath hiding the wood). Pale green broad forest canopy shapes and pale blue daylight visible THROUGH opaque glass. Crucial display constraint: final sprite will be only 90x98 physical pixels, so design as if drawing directly at 90x98. Use compact color clusters, clear broad outlines, very few broad shading steps, no tiny foliage, no intricate carving, no noise, no hairline vines or ornamental microtexture. Remain a warm handcrafted painted game asset matching the approved detailed forest bed, not a severe coarse pixel prototype. Exactly one complete window centered with transparent padding. True alpha outside silhouette, opaque window panes. No wall, no room, no floor, no text or labels, no background checkerboard, no external cast shadow. If supported output directly at 90x98 pixels; otherwise keep the drawing suitable for exact reduction to that size.

prompts.name: window-forest-night-v1
prompts.prompt: Use case: lighting-weather. Asset type: NIGHT variant of this exact transparent forest window game sprite. Edit target is input image 1. Change ONLY the view THROUGH the four glass panes from daytime to nighttime: dark muted blue-green woodland canopy silhouettes, deep desaturated navy sky and gentle cool moonlight. Preserve the exact outer alpha silhouette, all frame and leaf positions, right-wall projection, crop, framing, mullions and ornament geometry so day and night assets align. Keep honey wood and sage leaves readable with muted nighttime tones, no bright yellow sunlight, no rim glow or halo. Do not add moon or stars in front of frame, do not add props, curtains, labels or characters. True transparent alpha outside the window. This sprite will be exported at 90x98 physical game pixels, so use broad simple canopy shapes and few clear shading regions, no tiny leaves or noisy texture. The night version should be the same furniture with only night lighting and glass scenery changed.
